observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. South: a low, flat creature seen from the front. Its top is a broad slab of cracked tan clay plates with cracks radiating from a central point. Under the front rim are two hooded eyes and a long horizontal mouth slit, with four stubby, many-toed feet below. East: a much longer side profile of the same flat cracked-clay slab over a scaly, low-slung body. It has three visible feet, and a head at the right end is tucked under the rim, with one narrow eye and a long jaw slit. North: the same radial-cracked slab with the rear rim toward the camera, two hind feet in front, smaller feet at the sides, and no face. All three are about the same height. South and north are about the same width.
observed.south.png: Front view at full resolution. The cracked clay carapace is seen at an oblique angle from above, and its radial cracks meet at a reddish centre. Under the front edge sit two deep-set, heavy-lidded eyes in shadow and a wide dark mouth slit lined with a fine comb- or baleen-like fringe. Four broad, pebbly feet with blunt toes. The skin is pebbly brown like dried mud. Painterly and realistic, with no gloss or smile. Clean alpha with no ground shadow.
observed.east.png: Side profile. The long flat slab is wider than it is deep. A pebbly, scaled flank and lower body run beneath it, with fore and hind legs splayed outward. The head at the right end is a flattened, crocodilian-length snout fused under the slab, with a narrow hooded eye and a long jaw-line showing a strainer fringe. At the left end the body stops at the hind leg, with no tail visible. Painterly, realistic texture. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Rear view. The carapace is seen at the same oblique angle, with the radial cracks centred. The rear rim has a broken-plate edge. Two hind legs face the camera, with toes pointing roughly toward the viewer, and the side legs are partly visible. No eyes, mouth or face. The pebbly texture looks slightly stretched sideways (consistent with the 1.253x horizontal stretch), but it is not obvious at normal zoom. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature is about 4 cells long beside a vanilla human about 1 cell tall. It is low, roughly human-chest height, and very long and broad. At 32 px per cell it reads as a flat tan cracked-clay disc on stubby legs, several times the human's length. It reads as a patch of cracked ground on legs.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the front rim with two eyes and the mouth slit facing the camera, and four feet below.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the rear rim of the carapace and the hind feet. There are no eyes, mouth or face anywhere.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings are oblique views from the side or front. The carapace top is seen at an angle and the legs and rim are visible, so none is a top-down view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The measured heights are 253, 255 and 251 px. South and north widths now match on the shared-scale panel.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The same radial-cracked clay slab, pebbly brown skin and stubby many-toed feet appear on every facing. The head appears on south and east and is correctly absent on north. The carapace turns with the body (wide on south and north, long on east).

SIGNATURE.seen: The defining feature, a clay-pan back with cracks radiating from one centre that is too regular, is the dominant read on every facing. The jaw-plate strainer fringe is visible in the mouth slit on south and east.

ALIEN.seen: The flat shell on four legs suggests a turtle. But it has no protruding head or neck, and the shell is a terrain-like cracked mud pan rather than scutes. The mouth is a full-width strainer slit under the rim. A stranger would more likely say 'cracked ground with legs' than name a turtle.

STYLE.seen: The eyes are now shadowed, deep-set and heavy-lidded, and the mouth is a dark slit, with no smile or glossy round eyes. The texture is painterly and realistic: pebbly skin and fractured clay with natural shading.

OURS.seen: This is a unique invented design with no vanilla or other-mod counterpart. The card's provenance says it is a polish of the project's own s1r3.

ALPHA.seen: The cut-out is clean on all three. Code reports real alpha, and there is no ground patch, shadow or halo.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: The two deferred notes are addressed. North now matches south in height and width (2% spread). The face no longer reads cartoonish: the eyes are hooded and set in shadow, and the mouth is a slit with a fringe.

SCALE.seen: It is about 4 cells long beside a 1-cell human and plainly a giant, as 'canyon-floor giant' requires. It is low and flat, which suits an animal that passes for terrain.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px per cell it reads as a single bold flat tan disc with radial cracks and a dark underside band and feet, distinct from the ground grid.

request.subject: RM_Muttavaq

edits.change: In the north view the animal is seen from behind. The rear edge of the slab is a plain, closed, cracked clay wall with no mouth and no eyes. Beneath it show only the heels and the backs of the two hind feet, pressed flat against the ground, with the toes pointing away from the viewer toward the front of the animal.

The cracked clay skin has one fixed grain on every facing: the same pebbly texture at the same scale, with the polygon plates keeping their size and proportion whether seen from the front, side or rear. Each foot, from any side, has the same broad, short, blunt, toeless column of clay with a flat sole.

The legs are four short, thick, column-like pillars of the same pale ochre clay, set well inward under the slab. The slab's thick edge hangs over them and hides most of each column, so from the side only a low strip of foot shows at the ground. The slab reads as a raised piece of canyon floor lifted on hidden supports, and its profile is a straight-sided tabletop with squared edges and a flat top.

The front edge of the slab is one continuous clay lip. The jaw-plate comb sits recessed in a long, straight, shadowed slit under this lip, and the plates are thin, pale, vertical and evenly spaced. The two eyes are tiny dark pinpoints sunk into the lip's clay and almost hidden, with no lids, no brow and no pupil highlight. The animal has the body of a living patch of terrain with a built-in strainer, a radial crack pattern across its top, and no head, neck or tail.

invariants: pale ochre and dusty tan dried-clay palette
single huge flat slab about four times as long as it is tall, with a level tabletop top
polygon plates on the top, separated by dark cracks radiating from one central point
long straight horizontal mouth slit with a dense fringe of thin vertical clay-coloured filter plates
no tusks, horns, fangs or teeth
exactly one creature, centred, whole body visible, transparent background, painterly vanilla RimWorld style with a clean dark outline
request.prompt: A creature sprite for RimWorld: the muttavaq, a huge alien canyon-floor animal that sleeps for years as a patch of dried clay pan. Its body is one enormous, flat, straight-sided slab of cracked clay, about four times as long as it is tall, with a level tabletop top and squared edges, like a raised block of canyon floor. The slab's thick edge hangs over four short, thick, column-like supports of the same pale ochre clay, set well inward under the slab. Only a low strip of broad, blunt, toeless foot with a flat sole shows at the ground, so the animal sits low and reads as terrain on hidden supports. There is no neck, head or tail. The front edge of the slab is one continuous clay lip, and under it opens a long, perfectly straight, horizontal, shadowed mouth slit, expressionless. The slit is recessed and filled with a dense comb of thin, flat, pale vertical filter plates, evenly spaced like baleen, a sieve for straining mud. Two tiny dark pinpoint eyes are sunk into the clay of the front lip above the slit, almost hidden, without lids or highlights. The whole flat top is a field of hard, regular polygon plates of dried cracked clay, separated by dark cracks that radiate outward from one central point on the top, more regular than natural mud. The skin, supports and plates all share one fixed pebbly grain at one scale, in the pale ochre and dusty tan of dried canyon clay. Facings: the front view shows the front lip, the eyes and the mouth slit toward the viewer, with the front feet seen head-on. The side view shows the long profile, with the mouth slit at the front end and the cracked top above. The rear view, seen from behind, shows a plain, closed, cracked clay wall with no mouth and no eyes, and beneath it the heels and the backs of the hind feet toward the viewer, with the toes pointing away toward the front of the animal. Realistic painterly vanilla RimWorld sprite style, soft painted edges in a deeper shade of the local colour, clean dark outline. Exactly ONE creature, centred, the whole body visible with nothing cut off. Fully transparent background: no ground, no water, no shadow, no text, no border.
